title: Evaluation Metrics in Classic Machine Learning Problems
description: A listing of different evaluation metrics for classification, regression, clustering, and association problems.
content:
**Evaluation metrics** are quantitative measures used to assess how well a machine learning model performs. The right metric depends on the type of problem: classification, regression, clustering, or association rule learning.

**Classification problems**

• Accuracy - the ratio of correctly classified instances out of the total number of instances. Not suitable for imbalanced datasets.
• Precision - the ratio of true positive predictions out of all positive predictions (i.e. true positives divided by the sum of true positives and false positives). Useful when the false positive error term is high.
• Recall - the ratio of true positive predictions out of all actual positive instances (i.e. true positives divided by the sum of true positives and false negatives). Useful when the false negative error term is high.
• F-score - the harmonic mean of precision and recall. Suitable for imbalanced datasets; the harmonic mean is useful because it gives attention to the lower value, whether of precision or recall.
• ROC AUC (Area under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve) - built by plotting the true positive rate (sensitivity or recall, the ratio of true positive predictions out of all actual positive instances) against the false positive rate (1 − specificity, the ratio of false positive predictions out of all actual negative instances). This approach is more effective when one deals with an imbalanced dataset.
• PR AUC (Area under the Precision-Recall curve) - built by plotting precision against recall. This approach is more effective when one deals with a balanced dataset.

**Regression problems**

• Mean absolute error (MAE) - the sum of absolute discrepancies between actual and predicted values. Useful for interpreting results, less sensitive to and robust against outliers, but mathematically it is not smooth.
• Mean squared error (MSE) - the sum of squared discrepancies between actual and predicted values. Useful for high outlier error terms; mathematically it is smooth, so gradient descent optimization can be applied.
• R2 metric (coefficient of determination) - quantifies how well a regression model explains the variance of the outcome. Calculated as 1 minus the ratio of the sum of squared residuals to the total sum of squares (i.e. the dataset variance).

**Clusterization problems**

• Silhouette Score - evaluates how similar instances are to each other within their clusters and how different they are from each other across clusters.
• Adjusted Rand Index - evaluates expected and predicted clusters, adjusting for randomness.

**Association problems**

• Support - says how popular an itemset is; it equals the frequency of a certain itemset within the dataset.
• Confidence - measures the conditional probability of seeing the consequent item given the antecedent; it says how likely item B is selected when item A is selected, and equals Support(A -> B) / Support(A).
• Lift - assesses the increase of the probability of the consequent when the antecedent is present; it says how likely item A is selected while controlling for how popular item B is, and equals Confidence(A -> B) / Support(B).
